content.value_statement: Deployment workflows can become slow, risky, and inconsistent. This skill helps design staged CI/CD pipelines with gates, checks, rollbacks, and release strategies.
actual_capabilities: Outlines source, build, test, staging, approval, production, verification, and rollback stages.
Compares manual, delayed, and multi-approver approval gate patterns.
Describes rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature-flag deployment strategies.
Shows CI/CD patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Kubernetes, and Argo Rollouts.
Defines monitoring metrics and health checks for post-deployment verification.
limitations: Does not provision infrastructure or execute deployment commands.
Examples use placeholder app names, URLs, and secrets.
Requires adaptation to each CI/CD provider and compliance policy.
Does not replace security review of production pipeline code.

use_cases.title: Create a New Release Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan stages, gates, checks, and rollback points before implementing provider-specific workflow files.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Delivery
use_cases.description: Define reusable deployment patterns for teams that need consistent staging, approval, and production workflows.

use_cases.title: Improve Release Governance
use_cases.description: Add approval gates, verification steps, and rollback criteria to reduce production release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a basic CI/CD pipeline for my application. Include build, test, staging, approval, production, verification, and rollback stages.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Deployment Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature-flag deployment for my service. Recommend one strategy with risks and required controls.

prompt_templates.title: Add Approval Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design approval gates for staging and production. Include required reviewers, automated evidence, deployment windows, and emergency bypass rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design Enterprise Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an enterprise deployment pipeline design for multiple services. Include GitOps flow, security checks, progressive delivery, observability, and rollback automation.

output_examples.input: Design a production pipeline for a web API.
output_examples.output: A staged deployment plan with build, tests, staging deploy, smoke tests, manual approval, canary production rollout, health checks, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Which rollout strategy should I use for a high-traffic service?
output_examples.output: A comparison of rolling, blue-green, and canary delivery with a recommendation based on traffic risk, infrastructure cost, and monitoring maturity.
A gate design that lists approval owners, required metrics, security scan evidence, timeout rules, and emergency deployment handling.

best_practices: Define stage gates and rollback criteria before writing provider-specific workflow syntax.
Store secrets in managed secret systems and pass them through approved CI/CD mechanisms.
Pair automated verification with human approval for high-risk production releases.
anti_patterns: Deploying directly to production without staging verification.
Copying example commands without replacing placeholders and access controls.
Treating approval gates as a substitute for tests, scans, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does this skill create pipeline files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides architecture guidance and examples. You still need to adapt and review workflow files for your environment.

faq.question: Which CI/CD systems does it cover?
faq.answer: It discusses patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Kubernetes, and Argo Rollouts.

faq.question: Can it help with approval workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers manual approvals, delayed approvals, and multi-approver production gates.

faq.question: Does it execute deployment commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and planning guidance. It does not run shell commands or contact external services.

faq.question: Can it help choose a rollout strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares rolling, blue-green, canary, and feature-flag deployment patterns.

faq.question: How should teams use the examples safely?
faq.answer: Treat examples as templates. Replace placeholders, review permissions, validate secrets handling, and test in non-production environments first.
